features.title: What you can do in Folio
features.subtitle: One place for what your team knows — and it stays yours.

git.title: Everything lives in Git
git.text: Every page is a Markdown file and every change is a commit. Connect your own repository and keep the whole history.

together.title: Write together, live
together.text: Several people edit a document, a table or a whiteboard at once, and see who else is on the page.

offline.title: Works offline
offline.text: Keep writing and creating pages without a connection. Everything syncs when it is back.

tables.title: Data tables and forms
tables.text: Typed columns, saved views, filters and sorting. A form collects answers straight into a table.

boards.title: Whiteboards and diagrams
boards.text: Draw on an Excalidraw canvas, or build a Mermaid diagram by clicking instead of writing code.

access.title: Access under control
access.text: Roles per space, access to a single page, share links for guests and an audit log.

ai.title: Meet Folio AI
ai.subtitle: An assistant that knows your wiki. It is optional: Folio works in full without it.

ask.title: Ask
ask.text: Ask a question and get an answer drawn from your pages. This mode only reads and changes nothing.

agent.title: Agent
agent.text: Ask it to write a page, fill in a table or draw a whiteboard. It can do only what you are allowed to do yourself.

rules.title: Your own rules for every space
rules.text: Pages in the .agent folder tell the assistant how your team writes and what it must follow.

mcp.title: Open to your own agents
mcp.text: An MCP endpoint with personal access tokens lets outside agents and scripts read and write the wiki.

art.question: Where do we describe the release checklist?
art.answer: On the “Release process” page: seven steps, the last one is the rollback plan.

ai.byos: Bring your own key: the assistant runs on your own Cursor or Claude API key. Connect one whenever you like — the account menu, “Folio AI”.

ssoAdmin.title: Single sign-on
ssoAdmin.intro: Let people sign in with your identity provider over OpenID Connect or SAML 2.0 (Keycloak, Authentik, Entra ID, Okta, Google, …). Register the URLs shown on each provider at the identity provider.
ssoAdmin.noFolioSecret: FOLIO_SECRET is not set: a client secret can't be saved here. Set FOLIO_SECRET, or define the provider with environment variables.
ssoAdmin.deleteBody_one: {{count}} account is linked to it; the link is removed (the account stays).
ssoAdmin.deleteBody_other: {{count}} accounts are linked to it; the links are removed (the accounts stay).
ssoAdmin.envHint: Defined by environment variables: change it there and restart.
ssoAdmin.testWaiting: Finish the sign-in in the popup window…
ssoAdmin.testOk: The provider answered. What Folio would use (nothing was created or linked):
ssoAdmin.jitHint: A person without an account gets one (no password, not an administrator) at their first sign-in.
ssoAdmin.enforceHint: People in the allowed domains can't use a password. Instance administrators keep an audited emergency sign-in at /login?local.
ssoAdmin.linkHint: An existing account is linked only when the provider says the email is verified and its domain is allowed.

groupSync.title: Group sync
groupSync.enableHint: The groups in the "{{claim}}" claim become Folio group memberships each time a person signs in through this provider. Memberships added by hand are never touched.
groupSync.mode: Match IdP groups to Folio groups
groupSync.mapping: Table: IdP group = Folio group slug (one per line)
groupSync.createMissing: Create groups that do not exist yet
groupSync.createMissingHint: A Folio group is created for an IdP group with no match, marked as coming from this kind of provider.
groupSync.hint: Empty = every group. Otherwise a list of prefixes ("folio-, team-") or a regular expression between slashes ("/^team-/"). Memberships from the provider are added and removed at each sign-in.

saml.idpHint: Describe the identity provider with its metadata (a URL Folio re-reads hourly, or the pasted XML), or with the entity ID, SSO URL and signing certificate. Fields you fill in win over the metadata.
saml.idpCert: IdP signing certificate(s), PEM or base64
saml.attrHint: Left at email / name / groups, the usual Entra ID, Okta, Keycloak and Google attribute names are recognized too. Without an email attribute, an email-format NameID is used.
saml.emailAuthoritative: The IdP is authoritative for these domains' emails
saml.emailAuthoritativeHint: SAML carries no "email verified" flag. Without this option, a person who already has a Folio account with the same email can't sign in through this IdP: they are told the provider isn't trusted to confirm emails. Turn it on only if the IdP owns the accounts of the allowed domains: their emails then count as verified, so the existing Folio account is linked on the first sign-in.
saml.allowIdpInitiatedHint: Lets people start from the IdP's app portal. Such a response answers no request of this browser, so it cannot be tied to it: leave off unless you need it.
saml.linkHint: An existing account is linked only when the IdP is marked authoritative and the email's domain is allowed. The identity is the IdP entity ID plus the NameID: use a persistent NameID.

scimAdmin.title: SCIM provisioning
scimAdmin.intro: Let the identity provider create, update and deactivate people and groups in Folio over SCIM 2.0. Paste the base URL and the token into its provisioning settings (Okta: SCIM connector base URL + HTTP header token; Entra ID: Tenant URL + Secret token).

scimAdmin.shownOnce: Copy the token now: it is shown only once.
scimAdmin.rotateBody: The current token stops working at once. Paste the new one into the identity provider.
scimAdmin.revokeBody: The token stops working. People and groups already provisioned stay as they are.
scimAdmin.auditLink: SCIM events in the audit log
scimAdmin.jitNote: While SCIM is on, accounts come only from SCIM: creating accounts at first sign-in is off for this provider.
scimAdmin.jitNoteOff: Generating a token turns off creating accounts at first sign-in for this provider: accounts then come from SCIM.
scimAdmin.jitIgnored: This provider's environment variables turn JIT on; it is ignored while SCIM is on.
scimAdmin.jitTurnedOff: Creating accounts at first sign-in was turned off: SCIM provides the accounts now.
